sentences.text: Mr. Ajit Kumar Mishra Mr. Abhishek Dey Mr. B. Pratap Singh ...for the Petitioner Photostat certified copy of the petition for joint compromise is taken on record.

This is an application wherein the petitioner has prayed for quashing of the proceedings being Kanksa Police Station case no. 182 of 2020 dated 19.8.2020 under Sections 406/420/120B of the IPC, presently pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate, 4th Court, Durgapur.
The allegation levelled against the present petitioner is based on a claim of Rs. 60,32,693/- in connection with the supply of 321.16 metric ton Sponge Iron by the complainant to the petitioner.

During pendency of the proceeding, the parties have amicably settled their dispute out of court and a petition for joint compromise has already been filed before the Trial Court wherein the complainant herein has stated that the parties have settled their dispute and the complainant have received the dues and he has no grievance against the accused person/petitioner herein and that the good and harmonious relationship have been restored between the parties.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in view of the amicable settlement, further continuance of the instant proceeding will be mere abuse of process of the court and he prays for quashment of the proceeding.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the application is admitted.
Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of the application upon the State through the office of Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta and upon the opposite party no. 2 by speed post intimating the next date of hearing and to file affidavit of service on the returnable date.
Let the matter appear on 22nd April, 2026 under the heading "To Be Mentioned".
Learned counsel for the petitioner also prays for interim relief.
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioner and that the matter has already been settled between the parties, the impugned order dated 25th June, 2025 by which the court below has issued warrant of arrest against the present petitioner, shall be stayed for period of twelve weeks or until further order, whichever is earlier.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, be given to the parties upon compliance of all requisite formalities.
